question: Find the vector equation of the plane passing through the line of intersection of planes $P_1: \vec{r}\cdot(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) = 1$ and $P_2: \vec{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k}) = -4$, perpendicular to $P_3: \vec{r}\cdot(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}) = 0$.
solution:
1. Equation of family of planes: $\vec{r} \cdot [(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) + \lambda(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-\hat{k})] = 1 - 4\lambda$.
2. Normal vector $\vec{n} = (1+2\lambda)\hat{i} + (1+3\lambda)\hat{j} + (1-\lambda)\hat{k}$.
3. Perpendicularity with $P_3$: $\vec{n} \cdot (\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}) = 0 \implies (1+2\lambda) - (1+3\lambda) + (1-\lambda) = 0$.
4. Yields $\lambda = 0.5$. Substituting gives the plane: $4x + 5y + z + 2 = 0$.
